A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RESfM work despite the revised title and formatting. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original MegaDepth and 1DSFM reconstruction experiments, camera-pose errors, classification results and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V2 reports original reconstruction experiments on four datasets, expanded baseline comparisons, resource measurements and component ablations.

M1.justification: The stated robust bundle-adjustment procedure changes from three rounds to two: v2 Section 3.5 omits v1 Section 3.3's final restoration and triangulation of discarded tracks followed by another BA round. The encoder, prediction heads, losses and basic fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation on four Strecha scenes and four BlendedMVS scenes, extending coverage to small image collections with measured ground truth and synthetic rendered/blended imagery. MegaDepth training and evaluation, together with 1DSFM generalization tests, remain.

E2.justification: V2 adds GASFM, Theia and GLOMAP to the MegaDepth/1DSFM accuracy comparisons, and evaluates VGGSfM and MASt3R on the new benchmarks. COLMAP disappears from the original datasets' pose-accuracy tables, although it remains in runtime comparisons and the new benchmark tables.

E3.justification: V2 introduces ground-truth-pose evaluations using a 0.8 outlier threshold for Strecha/BlendedMVS, new classifier and frozen-encoder controls, and standard-versus-robust BA comparisons. It adds camera-throughput and resource metrics while dropping reprojection error from reported evaluation. The original training splits and 1000-epoch fine-tuning budget are retained.

E4.justification: V1 contains classification diagnostics and reconstruction examples but no component ablations. V2 Section 4.5 and Appendix D add PointNet versus sets-of-sets classification, frozen versus jointly trained encoder, and standard versus robust BA experiments (Tables 7, 8 and 11). Table 7 also measures residual outliers after BA.

E5.justification: V2 Appendix B newly specifies a fixed seed of 20; v1 provides no seed. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or comparable uncertainty estimates. This is additional seed disclosure, not evidence of increased replication.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive benchmark, baseline, resource and ablation results, removes reprojection-error results and the MegaDepth 0205 row, and revises existing scores. For example, scene 5016 changes from 16.9% outliers and 4.46 degrees mean rotation error to 0.2% and 0.12 degrees in the respective Table 1s. The PDFs do not establish this as a same-setting gain.

T1.justification: The calibrated, stationary-scene assumptions, permutation-equivariant map and loss equations remain substantively unchanged. V2's added rank-four projective-factorization discussion supplies background motivation rather than a new derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The central claim of robust deep SfM for large, contaminated image collections remains. V2 broadens comparative claims beyond ESFM to existing deep methods, describes parity with leading classical methods instead of broadly emphasizing speed superiority, and explicitly lists the prepared benchmark among its contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations about the importance of jointly training the encoder and using sets-of-sets rather than PointNet classification. It qualifies accuracy comparisons by noting fewer reconstructed cameras and explains camera exclusion through disconnected viewing graphs. V1's explicit warning about very high outlier ratios is omitted.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies loss weight alpha = 10, A40 memory capacity, similarity alignment for evaluation, and the expanded threshold search. It loses v1's precise checkpoint criterion of minimum post-BA reprojection error. Both versions retain the same future-release statement for code and preprocessed data.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around projective factorization, global SfM and recent deep reconstruction pipelines. It discusses Theia, GLOMAP, VGGSfM, DUSt3R, MASt3R, ACE-Zero and FlowMap, while removing the NeRF/implicit-surface background. These changes broaden the substantive comparison with prior research.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively rewritten around projective factorization and an explicit contribution list. Related work and results are reorganized, the loss section precedes inference, training information moves into a main-text subsection, and qualitative examples and median results move into expanded appendices.

P2.justification: V2 redesigns the architecture figure, replaces input-photo panels with GASFM reconstruction comparisons, and reorganizes qualitative figures. Pose tables combine rotation and translation, separate means from appendix medians, and introduce colored comparison highlights. New benchmark, resource and ablation tables substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important validation gaps in v1 through ground-truth benchmarks, broader competitive baselines and controlled component ablations. These substantially strengthen evidence for generalization and the design choices. Removed reprojection and large-dataset COLMAP accuracy results, plus reporting inconsistencies such as Theia camera counts across Tables 2 and 5, are drawbacks, but the validation gains outweigh them.
